title: FIRST_TRANCHE24 target deduplication and alias policy

const.definition: same canonical artifact identity claim and same version-form claim; repeated locator or record only
const.canonical_representative_rule: retain one representative and preserve every duplicate candidate disposition

const.definition: different locator or naming token explicitly declared to identify the same artifact by governed evidence
const.canonical_representative_rule: retain the explicitly identified canonical representative; never infer from naming

const.definition: copy hosted at a different locator with an explicit origin-to-mirror relationship
const.canonical_representative_rule: mirror is noncanonical unless a governed relationship identifies the canonical origin
const.evidence_required: explicit origin, mirror, and same-version relationship evidence

const.definition: related project or copied object with a distinct identity, owner, lineage, or modification history
const.canonical_representative_rule: retain as distinct; reject as canonical unless governed authority explicitly binds it

const.definition: transformed, filtered, repackaged, or generated output derived from another artifact
const.canonical_representative_rule: retain as distinct derivative and do not collapse into the source artifact
const.evidence_required: derivation evidence when relation is claimed

const.definition: same artifact identity with a different immutable version claim
const.canonical_representative_rule: retain each version separately; do not choose a version in target resolution
const.evidence_required: artifact identity equality and version distinction

const.definition: similar name, topic, layout, domain, or content without an explicit identity relationship
const.canonical_representative_rule: retain as separate and reject from canonical resolution unless independently eligible
const.evidence_required: none; lack of relation is sufficient

const: exact duplicates may collapse only after exact identity and version equality
aliases and mirrors may collapse only after explicit relationship evidence
forks, copies, derivatives, and version variants remain distinct candidates
every enumerated candidate receives an explicit disposition and reason
a disposition cannot convert a noncanonical mirror into canonical authority
unproven mirror or alias relationship remains separate and cannot be selected as canonical
normalization equality alone is not authority evidence
no candidate may be deleted from the set without a recorded disposition
a relationship conflict or multiple representatives prevents automatic uniqueness
